# hetznerrobot_server_addon_order (Resource)

Orders an addon for a server — an additional IPv4 address, a subnet or a failover subnet (`hetznerrobot_server_addon_products`). The new IP or subnet appears in `resources` once the order is ready.

~> **Destroying this resource does not cancel anything.** It only removes the order from state; what was ordered keeps running and is billed until it is cancelled.

Ordering through the webservice has to be enabled in Robot first (Administration → Settings → Web service settings → Ordering). Robot accepts 20 orders per day; prices are in the account's currency (`hetznerrobot_currency`). Create waits for the transaction to become `ready` (see `timeouts`). When the wait ends early the order stays placed: the apply finishes with a warning, and a later refresh fills in what is still missing — it never orders twice. Robot keeps transactions for 30 days; after that the state simply stays as it is.

Cancel an IP with `hetznerrobot_ip_cancellation`, a subnet with `hetznerrobot_subnet_cancellation`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An additional IPv4 address for server 321. Destroying this resource does NOT
# cancel the IP — use hetznerrobot_ip_cancellation for that.
resource "hetznerrobot_server_addon_order" "extra_ip" {
  server_number = 321
  product_id    = "additional_ipv4"
  reason        = "Virtual machines with public addresses"
}

output "extra_ip" {
  value = one([for r in hetznerrobot_server_addon_order.extra_ip.resources : r.id if r.type == "ip"])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `product_id` (String) Addon product id, e.g. `additional_ipv4`, `subnet_ipv4_29` or `failover_subnet_ipv4_29`.
- `server_number` (Number) Server the addon is ordered for.

### Optional

- `gateway` (String) Routing target of a `subnet_ipv4` addon: one of the server's additional IPv4 addresses. Defaults to the server's main IP.
- `reason` (String) RIPE reason — why the addresses are needed. Robot requires it for the product types `ip_ipv4`, `subnet_ipv4` and `failover_subnet_ipv4`.
- `test` (Boolean) When true, Robot validates the order but does not process it — nothing is ordered or billed, and no server number is ever assigned. **This is the documented behaviour; the provider's ordering has not been run against the live API yet.** Send one test order by hand first and check in Robot that nothing was ordered.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `date` (String) Date the order was placed.
- `product_name` (String) Name of the ordered addon.
- `product_type` (String) Type of the ordered addon, e.g. `ip_ipv4`.
- `resources` (Attributes List) What the order created, once ready — e.g. `{type = "ip", id = "203.0.113.7"}`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `status` (String) Transaction status: `in process`, `ready` or `cancelled`.
- `transaction_id` (String) Id of the order transaction.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Id of the resource — the IP address or the subnet's network address.
- `type` (String) Type of the resource, e.g. `ip` or `subnet`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Works only while Robot still keeps the transaction (30 days).
tofu import hetznerrobot_server_addon_order.extra_ip B20261012-1843193-S33055
```
